1	# SMA-769: OpenAI Responses API ingress and tool-call interception (`/v1/responses`)
2	
3	Linear: SMA-769 (parent SMA-747). Blocked by SMA-757 (merged in `ed5409fd`). Related: SMA-749 (the
4	tool-call model, the interceptor and the oracle), SMA-750 (Anthropic ingress), SMA-752 (policy
5	decisions), SMA-753 (sequence rules), SMA-755 (decision log).
6	
7	This spec extends SMA-749 (`2026-11-09-sma-749-tool-call-assembler-design.md`) and SMA-757
8	(`2026-11-14-sma-757-oracle-argument-prefix-design.md`). Every rule of those two specs applies to
9	the new format unless this spec says otherwise. A reference in the form "749 § 4.3" points to
10	them. The spec challenge of 2026-11-14 is in § 14.
11	
12	## 1. Intent
13	
14	The gateway serves only `POST /v1/chat/completions`. A client that sends `POST /v1/responses`
15	cannot use the gateway, so its tool calls are not intercepted.
16	
17	The newest OpenAI models need the Responses API for tools. On `/v1/chat/completions`, a `gpt-6`
18	model accepts function tools only with `reasoning_effort: "none"`. `gpt-6.1-sol` and `gpt-6-astra`
19	do not accept `none`, so they cannot stream tool calls on Chat Completions at all (757 § 2.4).
20	
21	This change adds `POST /v1/responses`. It has the same authentication, rate limits, budget charge
22	and tool-call interception as `/v1/chat/completions`, for streamed and non-streamed responses.
23	SMA-749 lists the Responses API as a non-goal. This spec removes that non-goal.
24	
25	## 2. Threat model and invariant
26	
27	The threat model of 749 § 2 applies unchanged: T1 hostile model output, T2 a non-conforming
28	upstream, T3 the caller is not an adversary of its own agent.
29	
30	**Invariant (I1, Responses form).** For every supported client parser P (§ 10.1), every tool call
31	that P derives from the bytes the gateway emits was decided `Allow`, with the same output index,
32	call id, kind, namespace, name and arguments that the decider saw. "Tool call" means every output
33	item that the **client** runs (§ 6.2), on every surface where P exposes it. Anything the gateway
34	cannot classify with certainty is not forwarded (or triggers `on_failure`).
35	
36	The SMA-757 rule D2 applies from the start: at an excused client raise, every call in the client's
37	snapshot must match an allowed call exactly. A prefix of allowed arguments is a failure.
38	
39	## 3. Read state (2026-11-14, `origin/main` `ed5409fd`)
40	
41	### 3.1 The gateway today
42	
43	- Only `/v1/chat/completions` has a route (`adapters/http/mod.rs:107`). `/v1/messages` (SMA-750)
44	  is not wired. The Anthropic format exists only as library code.
45	- The service code is chat-specific in five places: `interception::intercept_body` (fixed to
46	  `Format::OpenAiChat`), `interception::intercepted_stream` (fixed to OpenAI and
47	  `TERMINAL_SSE_ERROR`), `OpenAiClient::chat_completion` (fixed upstream path),
48	  `usage::request_tokens_estimate` (reads `messages`), and `dto::ChatCompletionRequest` (requires
49	  `messages`).
50	- `UsageScanner` reads `/usage/total_tokens` per record, and it skips any record over
51	  `MAX_RECORD_BYTES = 64 KiB` without a parse (`usage.rs:11`, `:122-126`). `non_stream_usage` reads
52	  only `choices[]` (`usage.rs:65`).
53	- The interceptor treats a record over `max_record_bytes` (1 MiB) as a stream failure, even with an
54	  empty queue (`interceptor.rs:234-237`). `max_request_bytes` defaults to 1 MiB
55	  (`config.rs:438`).
56	- `json.rs` `DATA_KEYS` is `["input", "input_schema", "parameters"]`. Below a `DATA_KEYS` key,
57	  `parse_strict` relaxes the envelope key rules (`case_folded_key`, `constructor`, `prototype`).
58	  The body path runs `check_numbers` over the whole body (`body.rs:36`).
59	- The stream capability is `stream_enabled` in config, advertised as
60	  `Capability::GatewayChatStream`.
61	- The oracle maps every kind that it does not list to `"other"` (`oracle.rs:89-97`), and
62	  `arguments_match` returns `true` for `"other"` (`:118-121`). `runners()` falls back to the chat
63	  runners with a `_ =>` arm (`:81-85`). `check_i1` matches calls by choice, kind, name and
64	  arguments (`:158`).
65	
66	### 3.2 Client SDKs (read from source; nothing was executed)
67	
68	Versions: **openai-python 3.48.0**, **openai-node 7.57.0**, **langchain-openai 1.8.0 with
69	langchain-core 1.8.0**. In openai-python, `_streaming.py` and
70	`lib/streaming/responses/_responses.py` are byte-identical in 3.40.0 (the version that 757 cites)
71	and 3.48.0.
72	
73	| Aspect | openai-python 3.48.0 | openai-node 7.57.0 | LangChain 1.8.0 |
74	|---|---|---|---|
75	| Dispatch key | `data.type`; `event:` ignored | `data.type`; `event: error` raises | `chunk.type` (python raw stream) |
76	| Top-level truthy `error` key | raises | raises | raises (python) |
77	| Leading BOM | not stripped | stripped | as python |
78	| Last event with no blank line at EOF | dropped | flushed | as python |
79	| `[DONE]` | prefix match, stop | exact match, stop | as python |
80	| `error` event (`type: error`) | passed through | raises | raises |
81	| `response.failed` | passed through; `get_final_response()` raises | accumulated | raises |
82	| Unknown event type | passed through | raises (11 types ignored) | ignored |
83	| `item: null` on `added` | skipped | skipped | `AttributeError` |
84	| Keying | `output_index` | `output_index`; `item_id` must equal the item `id` | `item_id` first, then `output_index` |
85	| `*.done` events | stored apart; the live snapshot is unchanged | replace arguments, input or the whole item | ignored for `function_call`; used for `custom_tool_call` |
86	| Terminal `response.output` | the final response | replaces the whole snapshot | ignored for tool calls |
87	| Final call source | terminal `output` | the snapshot (partial at a clean EOF) | `added.arguments` + deltas (+ custom `done`); built-ins as content blocks |
88	| Item type check | none at terminal for a done index | skips an index it cannot find (`ResponseStream.mjs:244-250`) | none (`base.py:5615-5631`) |
89	
90	The `ResponseStreamEvent` union of openai-python 3.48.0 has 59 members. With `keepalive` it has 60,
91	which equals the Node set (`response-accumulator.mjs:242-303`).
92	
93	Consequences:
94	
95	- R-a. The SDKs read a call from **different events**. Python reads the terminal `output`. Node
96	  reads the last of `arguments.done`, `output_item.done` and the terminal event. LangChain reads
97	  `added.arguments` plus the deltas. All of these views must agree, or a client runs a call that
98	  the decider did not see (the Responses form of 749 D9).
99	- R-b. No SDK checks that an index keeps its item type across views. An index that is added as
100	  `message` and arrives as `custom_tool_call` at `done`, or as `function_call` in the terminal
101	  `output`, becomes a call in all three SDKs.
102	- R-c. LangChain's `tool_calls` hold a partial call at every prefix (`parse_partial_json`). A call
103	  must never be released before it is decided.
104	- R-d. Python fills a missing `response.output` on `response.failed` and `response.incomplete`
105	  from its partial items. A terminal event without an explicit `output` array exposes partial
106	  calls.
107	- R-e. LangChain appends a `function_call_arguments.delta` to the tool call chunk at its index,
108	  whatever the item type. A delta event on a `custom_tool_call` or `message` item becomes call
109	  data.
110	- R-f. LangChain's source says that real traffic can report a later `output_index` on an item's
111	  `done` events than on its `added` event, after several built-in tool calls (`base.py:5419-5421`).
112	  This is not measured (M3).
113	- R-g. Every lifecycle event carries the whole `response` object. It echoes `instructions`,
114	  `tools`, `text.format.schema` and `metadata`, and the terminal event repeats every output item.
115	  These events can be large.
116	
117	### 3.3 To measure in the implementation (§ 10.5, the first task)
118	
119	- M1. A continuation with `previous_response_id` after a function call that the client did not
120	  answer. Expected: a 400 error. This is a reason for D3. D3 stays whatever the result, because
121	  the gateway still cannot see the earlier turns.
122	- M2. Whether OpenAI sends `event:` lines, `[DONE]`, `sequence_number`, `obfuscation`, a wire
123	  `output_text`, and `keepalive` events on Responses streams, and the position of each.
124	- M3. Whether the events of one output item are contiguous, and whether `output_index` stays the
125	  same from `added` to `done` (R-f). Include a stream with several provider-run tool calls.
126	- M4. The `added`, delta and `done` shapes of each client-run kind that can be recorded: whether
127	  `function_call` `added` carries `arguments: ""`, and whether `computer_call`,
128	  `apply_patch_call`, `shell_call` and `local_shell_call` are complete at `added`.
129	- M5. What OpenAI emits when `max_output_tokens` cuts a function call: an `output_item.done` with
130	  `status: "incomplete"`, or no `done`.
131	- M6. A next turn after a rewrite: replay a rewritten output (a `reasoning` item followed by the
132	  `msg_paigasus_…` message) as `input`, with and without `store`, with
133	  `include: ["reasoning.encrypted_content"]`. Expected unknown. If OpenAI rejects it, the rewrite
134	  (§ 6.5) changes before implementation.
135	- M7. The byte size of `response.created` and `response.completed` with a long `instructions`
136	  (about 50 KB) and 30 tool schemas.
137	
138	## 4. Decisions
139	
140	| Id | Question | Decision |
141	|----|----------|----------|
142	| D1 | Where the format lives | A new module `paigasus-gateway-core::responses` (`classify`, `assembly`, `stream`, `body`), with its own `Protocol` implementation. It shares only the generic parts: `json`, `sse`, `report`, `interceptor`, `body`, `turn`. `ChoiceAssembly` does not change. |
143	| D2 | New core types | `Format::OpenAiResponses`. `HoldKey::Response` (one hold per response, D10). New `ToolCallKind` variants: `Computer`, `LocalShell`, `Shell`, `ApplyPatch`, `ToolSearch`, `McpApprovalRequest`. `function_call` uses `Function`, `custom_tool_call` uses `Custom`. `ToolCall` gets `namespace: Option<String>`. |
144	| D3 | Server-side state | **Stateless only.** With interception enabled (the global `[tool_interception] enabled`, that is `AppState.tool_interception` is `Some`, known before admission), a request is refused with 400 `responses-stateful-not-supported` when it has a non-null `previous_response_id`, `conversation` or `prompt`, or an `item_reference` input item. |
145	| D4 | Background mode | `background: true` is refused with the same 400, whether interception is enabled or not. The gateway has no route for `GET /v1/responses/{id}`, so a background result cannot be fetched through it. |
146	| D5 | `store` | The request body is forwarded unchanged. The gateway does not set `store: false`. D3 already stops every later turn from reading the stored output. A rewrite of `store` would be the first request rewrite (749 non-goal). Operator note: with `store` true, OpenAI keeps the output, including a blocked call, for its retention period (§ 9). |
147	| D6 | Service shape | One generic handler pipeline with an endpoint descriptor per route (§ 8). `/v1/chat/completions` moves to it with no change in behaviour. The descriptor is for OpenAI-shaped routes. SMA-750 decides whether it extends it. |
148	| D7 | Upstream | `OpenAiClient` gets one method that takes a closed `UpstreamRoute` enum (`ChatCompletions`, `Responses`), never a free path. `Responses` forwards to `{base_url}/v1/responses` with the same headers, timeouts and cancellation as chat. |
149	| D8 | Route switch | A new `[responses] enabled` config key, default `false`. When it is `false`, `/v1/responses` returns 404. Rollback is this key, with no deploy. |
150	| D9 | Streaming switch | Streaming obeys the existing `stream_enabled`. No new capability is advertised (749 D28). |
151	| D10 | The hold | **One hold per response.** It opens at the first client-run item's `added` frame and completes at the terminal event. The decider gets every client-run call of the response in one `decide` call, as it gets every call of choice 0 in chat. A truncation (§ 6.4, R15) blocks every call of the hold with `Truncated`. |
152	| D11 | Output framing | Re-framed as in 749 D3, with an `event: <data.type>` line before each `data:` line. `unframed()` uses the same form. `[DONE]` has no `event:` line. |
153	| D12 | Rewrite | A blocked item becomes a `message` item at the same `output_index`, frame by frame (§ 6.5). No other index changes. |
154	| D13 | Abort frame | A new constant for this format: `"\n\nevent: error\ndata: {\"type\":\"error\",\"code\":\"upstream-error\",\"message\":\"upstream stream error\",\"param\":null}\n\n"`. The leading blank line ends a partly sent record, as in `TERMINAL_SSE_ERROR`. |
155	| D14 | Billing | A Responses usage reader (§ 8.2) with no 64 KiB record limit. 749 D24 applies: a rewrite does not change the charge. |
156	| D15 | Size limits | Per-format limits. For Responses: `max_record_bytes` 16 MiB, `max_held_bytes` 32 MiB, and a separate `[responses] max_request_bytes` of 16 MiB. These are first values. M7 checks them, and the plan records the measured sizes. |
157	| D16 | Strict JSON | Per-format data subtrees and classifier keys (§ 7.1). The chat and Anthropic lists do not change (AC 8). |
158	| D17 | Request side | `parse_request(Format::OpenAiResponses, …)` builds `TurnFacts` (§ 7.2). |
159	| D18 | Client-run built-in items | Enforced like function calls (§ 6.2). They are held, decided and rewritten. |
160	
161	### Reasons
162	
163	- **D1.** Responses streams are item-based: each event has an `output_index` and an `item_id`, and
164	  `*.done` events repeat the full value. Chat Completions streams index-delta fragments. A shared
165	  assembly would put Responses cases into the code path that SMA-757 proved.
166	- **D3.** The gateway cannot see a turn that OpenAI stores. A decision then has no `prior_calls` or
167	  `tool_results`, and SMA-753 sequence rules fail open. A blocked call also stays in OpenAI's
168	  stored output, which the client never saw (M1). A `prompt` template can add tools that the
169	  gateway cannot see. With interception off, the gateway is a plain proxy, and these fields do no
170	  harm through it.
171	- **D8.** Billing and availability depend on shapes that are first measured in this change (M2,
172	  M7). An operator must be able to turn the route off without a deploy.
173	- **D10.** SMA-752 and SMA-753 policies that limit the calls per turn need every call of the turn
174	  in one decision. Chat gives them that per choice. A hold per item would give them one call at a
175	  time. The cost: frames after the first client-run item wait until the terminal event. Chat has
176	  the same cost until `finish_reason`.
177	- **D12.** A replacement at the same index keeps every later `output_index` valid. It needs no
178	  renumbering, which is the main cost of the chat rewrite.
179	- **D14, D15.** R-g. A lifecycle event over 64 KiB would charge only the estimate. A lifecycle
180	  event over 1 MiB would fail the stream, and every SDK raises without `response.created` or a
181	  terminal event. D3 also makes a client resend the whole conversation on every turn.
182	- **D18.** A shell command, a file patch or a mouse action has at least the risk of a function
183	  call. A report of "unenforceable" would let a client run an action that was never decided.
184	
185	## 5. Types
186	
187	```rust
188	pub enum Format { OpenAiChat, AnthropicMessages, OpenAiResponses }
189	pub enum HoldKey { Choice(u32), Block(u32), Response }
190	pub enum ToolCallKind {
191	    Function, Custom, LegacyFunctionCall, AnthropicToolUse, Other,
192	    Computer, LocalShell, Shell, ApplyPatch, ToolSearch, McpApprovalRequest,
193	}
194	pub struct ToolCall { /* 749 fields */ pub namespace: Option<String> }
195	```
196	
197	All stay `#[non_exhaustive]`. For a Responses call:
198	
199	| `ToolCall` field | Value |
200	|---|---|
201	| `choice` | `0` |
202	| `position` | the item's `output_index` |
203	| `id` | `call_id` (function, custom, computer, local shell, shell, apply patch, tool search); the item `id` for `mcp_approval_request` |
204	| `namespace` | `namespace` (function, when present); `server_label` (`mcp_approval_request`); `None` otherwise |
205	| `name` | `name` (function, custom, `mcp_approval_request`); a fixed label for the others: `computer`, `local_shell`, `shell`, `apply_patch`, `tool_search` |
206	| `arguments` | `arguments` (function; `""` becomes `"{}"`, as chat, 749 § 11); `input` (custom); for every other kind, including `Other`: the `done` item as compact JSON, with `status` removed |
207	
208	The chat and Anthropic formats set `namespace` to `None`. The notice and the report show
209	`<namespace>.<name>` when a namespace is present.
210	
211	## 6. The response stream
212	
213	### 6.1 Item-scoped event map
214	
215	Every item-scoped event type belongs to exactly one item type. The map is closed:
216	
217	| Event types | Item type |
218	|---|---|
219	| `response.content_part.*`, `response.output_text.*`, `response.refusal.*`, `response.output_text.annotation.added` | `message` |
220	| `response.reasoning_text.*`, `response.reasoning_summary_part.*`, `response.reasoning_summary_text.*` | `reasoning` |
221	| `response.function_call_arguments.*` | `function_call` |
222	| `response.custom_tool_call_input.*` | `custom_tool_call` |
223	| `response.shell_call_command.*` | `shell_call` |
224	| `response.mcp_call_arguments.*`, `response.mcp_call.*` | `mcp_call` |
225	| `response.mcp_list_tools.*` | `mcp_list_tools` |
226	| `response.web_search_call.*` | `web_search_call` |
227	| `response.file_search_call.*` | `file_search_call` |
228	| `response.code_interpreter_call.*`, `response.code_interpreter_call_code.*` | `code_interpreter_call` |
229	| `response.image_generation_call.*` | `image_generation_call` |
230	| `response.audio.*`, `response.audio.transcript.*` | no item (response-level) |
231	| `response.compaction.compacting` | `compaction` |
232	
233	The builder takes the exact type list from openai-python 3.48.0 and checks it against Node's
234	`expectedOutputItemTypes` (`response-accumulator.mjs:111-153`). An item-scoped event whose item
235	has another type is malformed.
236	
237	### 6.2 Item classes
238	
239	- **Tool-free content:** `message`, `reasoning`, `compaction`.
240	- **Provider-run, reported `unenforceable`, never decided:** `web_search_call`, `file_search_call`,
241	  `code_interpreter_call`, `image_generation_call`, `mcp_call`, `mcp_list_tools`, `program`,
242	  `program_output`, `additional_tools`, `tool_search_output`, `shell_call_output`,
243	  `local_shell_call_output`, `computer_call_output`, `apply_patch_call_output`. This is the
244	  treatment of Anthropic `server_tool_use` (749 § 4.2): the item opens no hold, its frames are
245	  forwarded in stream order (behind an open hold, 749 D12), and one report entry with
246	  `decision: "unenforceable"` is emitted. `on_failure` never applies to it.
247	- **Client-run (held and decided):** `function_call` (Function), `custom_tool_call` (Custom),
248	  `computer_call` (Computer), `local_shell_call` (LocalShell), `shell_call` (Shell),
249	  `apply_patch_call` (ApplyPatch), `tool_search_call` (ToolSearch), `mcp_approval_request`
250	  (McpApprovalRequest).
251	- **Any other item type**, including `function_call_output`, `custom_tool_call_output` and
252	  `mcp_approval_response` in the output: client-run, kind `Other` (fail closed).
253	
254	`shell_call` and `tool_search_call` are client-run for every value of `environment` and
255	`execution`. The class must be fixed at `added`, and these fields can be absent there. A hosted
256	shell or a server search then runs on the provider even when the decision is `block`. The report
257	says `block` for it, and the notice replaces it for the client. This is a known limit: the
258	SMA-755 log must not treat such a block as a prevented action (spec author's call).
259	
260	A `function_call` with a `caller` of type `program` is still a client-run `function_call`.
261	
262	### 6.3 Record classification
263	
264	Dispatch on `data.type`. A present `event:` name that differs from `data.type` is malformed. A
265	record with a top-level `error` key whose value is truthy, and a `type: "error"` record, are
266	upstream error records (749 D17 when a hold is open; forwarded otherwise). `[DONE]` ends the
267	stream. The known types are the 59 members of openai-python 3.48.0's `ResponseStreamEvent` union
268	plus `keepalive`. Any other type is malformed.
269	
270	### 6.4 Canonical rules (any deviation: stream-level `on_failure`, code `Malformed`)
271	
272	`keepalive` and the upstream error record are exempt from R1, R2 and R7.
273	
274	Stream order:
275	
276	- R1. The first record is `response.created`. Every lifecycle event has the same `response.id`.
277	- R2. `response.created`, `response.queued` and `response.in_progress` carry `response.output: []`.
278	- R3. Exactly one terminal event (`response.completed`, `response.incomplete` or
279	  `response.failed`). It carries `response.output` as an array, never absent or `null` (R-d).
280	  After it, only `[DONE]` may follow; `[DONE]` is then emitted. Any other record after it is
281	  dropped and counted (749 D4).
282	- R4. `output_index` values first appear in order 0, 1, 2, …, each on one
283	  `response.output_item.added`. Each index has exactly one `added` and at most one `done`.
284	- R5. The events of an item are contiguous: no event of another item arrives between its `added`
285	  and its `done` (M3).
286	- R6. Every item-scoped event has the `output_index` of the open item, and its `item_id` (where
287	  the type has one) equals that item's `id`. The event type matches the item type (§ 6.1).
288	- R7. `sequence_number`, when present, is an integer that strictly increases. Either every event
289	  has it or none does.
290	- R8. `added.item` is an object with a string `type` and a non-empty string `id`. Item `id`s are
291	  unique in the response, and `call_id`s are unique in the response. No upstream `id` starts with
292	  `msg_paigasus_`.
293	
294	Every item, of every class (R-b):
295	
296	- R9. `type`, `id`, `call_id`, `namespace` and `name` (each where the type has it) are equal in
297	  `added`, `done` and the item at the same index in the terminal `output`.
298	- R10. The terminal `output` has exactly one item per streamed `output_index`, in order, and no
299	  other item. An item with a `done` frame equals its `done` item as a JSON value in the terminal
300	  `output`.
301	
302	Per client-run item (R-a, R-e):
303	
304	- R11. `function_call`: `added.item.arguments` is `""`. The concatenated
305	  `function_call_arguments.delta` values equal `function_call_arguments.done.arguments`, which
306	  equals `done.item.arguments`. At `done`, the arguments are `""` or one complete JSON value
307	  (749 § 11 `incomplete_arguments`).
308	- R12. `custom_tool_call`: the same rule with `input` and `custom_tool_call_input.*`. `input` is
309	  free text.
310	- R13. `shell_call`: per command index i, the `shell_call_command.added` command plus its deltas
311	  equal its `shell_call_command.done` command, which equals `done.item.action.commands[i]`.
312	  Indexes appear in order. `added` and `done` are equal as JSON values except for `status` and
313	  `action.commands`.
314	- R14. The other client-run kinds: `added` and `done` are equal as JSON values, except for
315	  `status` (M4).
316	- R15. A client-run item whose `done` has a `status` other than `"completed"` is a truncation (M5).
317	  So are a terminal event, `[DONE]` or EOF while a client-run item has no `done`.
318	- R16. No event for an item arrives after its `done`.
319	
320	If a measurement (§ 3.3) shows that real traffic breaks a rule, the work stops and the spec
321	changes first. A rule is not loosened in code.
322	
323	### 6.5 Rewrite
324	
325	Only frames that contain a blocked item are re-serialized. A blocked item's frames are rewritten
326	one by one, so the rule works for a blocked hold, a truncated item, a hold limit and a stream that
327	fails while the item assembles (`Mode::Failed`):
328	
329	- The item's `added` frame becomes three events: `response.output_item.added` with the message
330	  item, `response.content_part.added` with an empty `output_text` part, and
331	  `response.output_text.delta` with the notice (§ 6.6).
332	- Every middle frame of the item is dropped.
333	- The item's `done` frame becomes `response.output_item.done` with the completed message. When the
334	  item has no `done` frame, this event is synthesized before the next frame of the stream (the
335	  terminal event, `[DONE]`, EOF or the D13 frame), as chat's `closing()` does.
336	- In the terminal event, the item at a blocked index is always replaced with the completed message.
337	  This replacement is exempt from R10.
338	
339	The exact JSON, with `<i>` the blocked `output_index`, `<n>` the notice, and `<s>` the
340	`sequence_number` of the replaced frame (the key is left out when R7 says none):
341	
342	```json
343	{"type":"response.output_item.added","output_index":<i>,"sequence_number":<s>,
344	 "item":{"type":"message","id":"msg_paigasus_<i>","role":"assistant","status":"in_progress","content":[]}}
345	{"type":"response.content_part.added","item_id":"msg_paigasus_<i>","output_index":<i>,"content_index":0,"sequence_number":<s>,
346	 "part":{"type":"output_text","text":"","annotations":[],"logprobs":[]}}
347	{"type":"response.output_text.delta","item_id":"msg_paigasus_<i>","output_index":<i>,"content_index":0,"sequence_number":<s>,
348	 "delta":"<n>","logprobs":[]}
349	{"type":"response.output_item.done","output_index":<i>,"sequence_number":<s>,
350	 "item":{"type":"message","id":"msg_paigasus_<i>","role":"assistant","status":"completed",
351	         "content":[{"type":"output_text","text":"<n>","annotations":[],"logprobs":[]}]}}
352	```
353	
354	The three events from one `added` frame repeat its `sequence_number`. The emitted numbers then do
355	not strictly increase. No SDK of § 3.2 reads `sequence_number` on a `create` stream (spec author's
356	call; the Python conformance test of § 10.2 confirms it for openai-python).
357	
358	No other field of the terminal event changes: `status`, `usage`, `incomplete_details` and `error`
359	stay as the upstream sent them. If M2 shows a wire `output_text` field, the builder adds the
360	notice to it and records this here. The Responses API has no `finish_reason`, so nothing else is
361	rewritten.
362	
363	**Non-stream.** The same replacement in the body's `output[]` (the completed message). 749 § 4.4
364	applies otherwise: one re-serialization, and the original bytes when nothing is blocked.
365	
366	### 6.6 Notice, names and report
367	
368	749 § 4.5 and § 4.6 apply. The notice is `[paigasus] tool call "<name>" was blocked (<code>).`.
369	`<name>` is `ToolCall.name`, prefixed with `<namespace>.` when a namespace is present, then
370	sanitized. In a report, `choice` is `0` and `position` is the `output_index`.
371	
372	## 7. Request side and strict JSON
373	
374	### 7.1 Strict JSON per format
375	
376	- The Responses data subtrees are: `tools[]` (whole entries), `text`, `metadata`, `instructions`,
377	  `prompt`, `reasoning`, and `input` (request); `response.tools`, `response.text`,
378	  `response.metadata`, `response.instructions`, `response.prompt` and `response.reasoning`
379	  (lifecycle events and the non-stream body). Below a data subtree, the `parse_value_strict` rules
380	  apply.
381	- `check_numbers` runs on the envelope and on each client-run item only, not on data subtrees.
382	- The Responses classifier keys (`type`, `output_index`, `item_id`, `call_id`, `item`, `output`,
383	  `arguments`, `input`, `name`, `namespace`, `id`, `delta`, `response`, `error`) are a per-format
384	  list. The chat and Anthropic lists do not change.
385	- A test shows that a structured-output schema with properties `Name`, `ID`, `Type` and
386	  `constructor`, a metadata key `Id` and a schema `maximum: 1e300` pass unchanged on stream and
387	  body.
388	
389	### 7.2 `TurnFacts`
390	
391	- The handler parses a copy of the body into a `ResponsesRequest` DTO: `model`, `input`, `stream`,
392	  `background`, `previous_response_id`, `conversation`, `prompt`, all `Option`, and the rest as
393	  `extra`. `input` is a string or an array. A body that is not a JSON object is a 400, as in chat.
394	- D3 and D4 are checked before `Limits::admit`, so a refused request is not counted or charged.
395	- `definitions` from `tools[]`: function and custom names (with `namespace` from `namespace`
396	  tools), and the built-in tool types.
397	- `prior_calls` from the client-run item types of § 6.2 in `input`. `tool_results` from
398	  `function_call_output`, `custom_tool_call_output`, `computer_call_output`,
399	  `local_shell_call_output`, `shell_call_output`, `apply_patch_call_output` and
400	  `mcp_approval_response`.
401	- `TurnFacts` gets a `definitions_complete: bool`. It is `false` when `tools[]` has a `tool_search`
402	  tool, or when `input` has an `additional_tools` or `tool_search_output` item: tools can then be
403	  added at run time. SMA-752 decides how a policy treats an incomplete set. The chat and Anthropic
404	  formats set it to `true`.
405	
406	## 8. Service
407	
408	### 8.1 The generic pipeline
409	
410	An endpoint descriptor per OpenAI-shaped route:
411	
412	```rust
413	struct Endpoint {
414	    route: UpstreamRoute,          // D7
415	    format: Format,
416	    parse: fn(&[u8], bool /* interception */) -> Result<RequestFacts, ApiError>, // DTO, D3, D4
417	    estimate: fn(&RequestFacts, usize) -> u64,
418	    usage: UsageReader,            // § 8.2
419	    terminal: &'static str,        // TERMINAL_SSE_ERROR or D13
420	    max_request_bytes: usize,      // D15
421	}
422	```
423	
424	The flow is the current chat flow (auth, body limit, parse, stream switch, `Limits::admit`,
425	`ChargeGuard`, `parse_request`, upstream, usage, interception, non-2xx pass-through), with each
426	chat-specific step taken from the descriptor. `relay`, `intercepted_stream` and `intercept_body`
427	take the `Format` and the terminal frame. The names are a shape, not a fixed API.
428	
429	`/v1/chat/completions` moves to the pipeline. Its behaviour must not change: every existing service
430	test and every core golden passes byte-identical.
431	
432	Log events and the `"chat completion metered"` event get an `endpoint` field.
433	`gateway_upstream_requests_total` gets an `endpoint` label, and the observability drift files are
434	updated.
435	
436	### 8.2 Usage and the charge
437	
438	- **Stream.** A Responses scanner reads a copy of the upstream bytes, as `UsageScanner` does
439	  (1 token per data record). For `response.completed`, `response.incomplete` and `response.failed`
440	  records, it reads `response.usage.total_tokens` with a streaming key scan that has no record size
441	  limit and holds no more than the scan state. The last value wins. Other records over 64 KiB are
442	  skipped, as today.
443	- **Non-stream.** `usage.total_tokens` from the original body. Fallback: the completion estimate
444	  from `output[].content[].text`, `output[].arguments` and `output[].input`, by the chat rule
445	  (`usage.rs`).
446	- **Request estimate.** By the chat rule, over `instructions`, the `input` string, and per `input`
447	  item: `content` text (string or `input_text` parts), `arguments`, `input` and `output`.
448	- Tests: a terminal event over 64 KiB and one over 1 MiB are charged their reported usage, with
449	  interception on and off.
450	
451	## 9. Error handling and operator notes
452	
453	| Case | Result |
454	|---|---|
455	| `[responses] enabled = false` | 404 |
456	| D3 or D4 field present | 400 `responses-stateful-not-supported`, before admission |
457	| Body is not a JSON object | 400, as chat |
458	| Body over `[responses] max_request_bytes` | 413, as chat |
459	| Rate limit or budget | 429, as chat |
460	| `stream: true` and `stream_enabled` off | the chat refusal, with the same code |
461	| Upstream non-2xx | forwarded verbatim, no charge, as chat |
462	| Malformed record, deviation, truncation, hold limits | 749 § 6, with the D13 frame |
463	| Malformed non-stream body under `block` | 502 `tool-interception-malformed-response`, as chat |
464	
465	Operator notes (in the gateway README): D5 retention; the hosted-execution limit of § 6.2; the
466	`[responses]` keys.
467	
468	## 10. Testing
469	
470	### 10.1 Oracle models
471	
472	Four models, each with its cited version and source paths in a doc comment. Each derives calls
473	from every surface its SDK exposes:
474	
475	- **openai-python 3.48.0 `ResponseStream`.** `_streaming.py`, `lib/streaming/responses/_responses.py`
476	  and `lib/_parsing/_responses.py`. Calls: the items of every yielded `output_item.added` (for
477	  client-run kinds other than function and custom) and `output_item.done` event, the `output` of a
478	  yielded `response.incomplete` or `response.failed`, and the `get_final_response()` output.
479	- **openai-python 3.48.0 raw stream** (`client.responses.create(stream=True)`). The same SSE
480	  decoder, no accumulation. Calls: the items of every yielded `output_item.done` and the terminal
481	  `output`. It raises only at the SSE layer, so it is stronger than the `ResponseStream` model at
482	  an excused raise.
483	- **openai-node 7.57.0.** `core/streaming.ts`, `lib/responses/ResponseStream.ts` and
484	  `internal/responses/response-accumulator.ts`. Calls: the final snapshot (partial at a clean
485	  EOF), plus every emitted `output_item.done` item.
486	- **LangChain (langchain-openai 1.8.0, langchain-core 1.8.0)** on the raw stream.
487	  `_convert_responses_chunk_to_generation_chunk`, `merge_lists`, `merge_dicts`, and
488	  `init_tool_calls` with `parse_partial_json`. Calls: `tool_calls` of the summed chunk, plus the
489	  content blocks for `computer_call`, `apply_patch_call`, `mcp_approval_request` and
490	  `tool_search_call` (`base.py:5596-5614`). `invalid_tool_calls` are not calls.
491	
492	Each model reproduces every raise path that § 3.2 and the source list, and stops there with the
493	calls of its snapshot (`Run{calls, error}`). The D2 rule applies at each raise.
494	
495	Oracle changes:
496	
497	- `check_i1` gets a `RESPONSES_RUNNERS` table. The `_ =>` fallback in `runners()` becomes a panic,
498	  so a missing format cannot pass with zero calls.
499	- Each new kind gets its own model kind. Its comparison is JSON equality of the item with `status`
500	  removed, after the normalisation of each SDK (LangChain: `model_dump(exclude_none=True)`). A
501	  model call also matches on `position`, `id` (call id) and `namespace`.
502	- A mutation proof: a changed `action.commands` in a `shell_call` `done` item, and a changed patch
503	  in an `apply_patch_call`, must make P1 fail.
504	
505	### 10.2 Real-SDK conformance
506	
507	The Python conformance package (`py/packages/paigasus-gateway-conformance`) gets golden tests for
508	the Responses goldens, run through the real openai-python 3.48.0 `ResponseStream` and raw stream.
509	The package already pins `openai==3.48.0` (`pyproject.toml:13`), so no dependency change is
510	needed. openai-node and LangChain are covered by the Rust models only, because neither is a
511	dependency of the repo today.
512	
513	### 10.3 Generators and properties
514	
515	- A `responses_scenario()` generator in `tests/support/streams.rs`: items of every class in § 6.2,
516	  every client-run kind, text and reasoning items, and chunk cuts.
517	- **Every client raise path and every rule of § 6.4 gets a generator quirk** (757 lesson). The
518	  list includes: an `event: error` name; a top-level `error` key; `[DONE]x`; an unknown event
519	  type; a repeated `output_index`; a delta before `added`; an `item_id` mismatch; an event on the
520	  wrong item type (a function delta on a custom or message item); an item type that changes at
521	  `done` or in the terminal `output`; a terminal item that never streamed; `item: null`; a
522	  duplicate `id` or `call_id`; an `msg_paigasus_` id; a non-empty `in_progress.output`; a terminal
523	  item with a new `name` or `namespace`; `added.arguments` not empty; a terminal `output` absent or
524	  `null`; a `response.failed` with an open item; an `error` event mid-item; a `done` with
525	  `status: "incomplete"`; invalid JSON arguments at `done`; a lifecycle `response.id` change; a
526	  BOM; a last event with no blank line; a `keepalive` without `sequence_number`.
527	- P1 and P2 hold over at least 10 000 generated cases (`ProptestConfig::with_cases(10_000)`).
528	- The observe-mode and allow-all agreement properties of 749 § 8.1 get a Responses variant.
529	- A property test of the oracle itself, as 757 § 7.2: a raise between two argument deltas must be
530	  an `Err`.
531	
532	### 10.4 Fixtures and goldens
533	
534	- Hand-built `responses/conforming` and `responses/malformed` sets, written by `make_fixtures.py`,
535	  with a row per malformed fixture in `malformed_shapes_follow_section_6`. A client-run kind that
536	  cannot be recorded (M4) gets a conforming fixture built from the openai-python 3.48.0 types.
537	- Goldens under `tests/golden/responses/`, with the manifest, under `block_named` and
538	  `on_failure=block`: a blocked function call with deltas, a blocked built-in with only `added`
539	  and `done`, a truncated item, and a blocked call after a reasoning item.
540	
541	### 10.5 Recordings and measurements (the first task)
542	
543	- `capture.py` gets `--api responses`. It keeps its key handling (key from a file, never printed).
544	- Scenarios: parallel functions, custom and function, forced custom, a reasoning item before a
545	  call, text only, structured output, several provider-run tools (web search) then a function,
546	  `max_output_tokens` inside a call, long `instructions` with 30 tools, and the M1 and M6
547	  continuations.
548	- Models: `gpt-6.1-sol` (no reasoning-effort override), `gpt-6.1-terra`, and one older model
549	  (`gpt-4.1`).
550	- The results of M1 to M7 go into § 3.3. Each kept recording is deterministic in the tests and
551	  passes with no deviation (`recorded_streams_pass_unchanged`).
552	- This task comes first, because R5, R11 and the rewrite (M3, M4, M6) are design rules.
553	
554	### 10.6 Service tests
555	
556	A `tests/responses_proxy.rs`: the route switch; authentication; rate limit and budget; the charge
557	from `response.usage` (streamed and non-streamed, including terminal events over 64 KiB and
558	1 MiB); the D3 and D4 refusals (with interception on and off); the upstream route; the
559	non-stream rewrite and the `paigasus-tool-decisions` header; the streamed interception; the D13
560	frame on an upstream error. The existing chat tests pass unchanged.
561	
562	## 11. Repo gates this change touches
563	
564	- The new error code `responses-stateful-not-supported` follows the 749 § 7 chain: the proto enum,
565	  codegen drift, `GatewayError`, `ci/error-registry/check.py` and the SDK `mapError`.
566	- The `endpoint` metric label: the observability drift files and `repo:promtool`.
567	- New config keys: the config tests and the Helm chart values (`charts/CLAUDE.md`).
568	- The full gate graph of the root `CLAUDE.md`, before the push.
569	
570	## 12. Acceptance criteria
571	
572	1. `POST /v1/responses` works streamed and non-streamed, with the authentication, limits and budget
573	   of chat, behind `[responses] enabled`.
574	2. The D3 and D4 refusals hold, before admission.
575	3. Every client-run item kind of § 6.2 is held, decided and rewritten. Every provider-run item is
576	   reported `unenforceable`.
577	4. The four oracle models exist, with cited versions. Every raise path and every rule of § 6.4 has
578	   a generator quirk. The mutation proof of § 10.1 fails P1 as required.
579	5. P1 and P2 hold over at least 10 000 generated cases.
580	6. Recorded Responses streams from at least one `gpt-6` model are fixtures and pass with no
581	   deviation.
582	7. The D2 rule (no partial call at a client raise) holds in the oracle.
583	8. `/v1/chat/completions` behaviour is unchanged: all existing tests and goldens pass
584	   byte-identical.
585	9. M1 to M7 are recorded in § 3.3, and the spec agrees with them.
586	10. A terminal event over 64 KiB is charged its reported usage.
587	11. The full gate graph (root `CLAUDE.md`) passes.
588	
589	## 13. Non-goals and left to the builder
590	
591	Non-goals:
592	
593	- Server-side state: `previous_response_id`, `conversation`, `prompt`, `background`,
594	  `item_reference` (D3, D4).
595	- Other Responses routes: `GET`/`DELETE /v1/responses/{id}`, `/v1/responses/{id}/input_items`,
596	  `/v1/responses/{id}/cancel`, `/v1/responses/compact`, `/v1/responses/input_tokens`.
597	- The Realtime and WebSocket modes.
598	- Request rewriting, including `store` (D5).
599	- Policy deciders (SMA-752), detectors (SMA-754), the decision log (SMA-755), MCP (SMA-756), the
600	  Anthropic ingress (SMA-750).
601	- Tool calls encoded inside text content (749 non-goal).
602	- openai-node and LangChain as real-SDK conformance dependencies (§ 10.2).
603	
604	Left to the builder:
605	
606	- Module, type and function names, and the shape of the endpoint descriptor (§ 8.1).
607	- Whether the Responses oracle models live in `oracle.rs` or in a new file.
608	- The exact key allowlists per event type, read from openai-python 3.48.0's types.
609	- The streaming key scan of § 8.2.
610	
611	## 14. Spec challenge (2026-11-14) — changelog
612	
613	Verdict: NEEDS REWORK (3 BLOCKER, 9 MAJOR, 11 MINOR, 3 QUESTION). Folded in:
614	
615	- BLOCKER, item class not fixed across views: R9 and R10 now apply to every item; the closed event
616	  map of § 6.1; R8 (`item` an object, unique ids); quirks.
617	- BLOCKER, usage from a large terminal event: § 8.2 scanner with no record size limit; the
618	  estimate and body fallback; tests over 64 KiB and 1 MiB (AC 10).
619	- BLOCKER, the oracle does not compare the new kinds: per-kind comparison, the `_ =>` panic, the
620	  mutation proof (§ 10.1).
621	- MAJOR: per-format data subtrees and classifier keys (§ 7.1); per-format size limits (D15, M7);
622	  the frame-by-frame rewrite with exact JSON and the truncated case (§ 6.5); the `shell_call`
623	  rule per command index (R13, M4); more recording scenarios and the `keepalive`/`error`
624	  exemption and `[DONE]` after the terminal event (R3, § 10.5); the next-turn measurement (M6);
625	  `namespace` and `server_label` in the identity (D2, § 5); `definitions_complete` (§ 7.2); four
626	  oracle models that cover every surface, with match on position and call id (§ 10.1); R11 keeps
627	  the chat rule `""` → `"{}"` (§ 5); the route switch (D8).
628	- MINOR: the event counts; `Option` DTO fields; the error-code gate chain (§ 11); the exact D13
629	  bytes; `unframed()` framing (D11); unique ids and the `msg_paigasus_` prefix (R8); the
630	  hosted-execution limit (§ 6.2); the closed `UpstreamRoute` (D7); the SMA-750 reuse claim removed
631	  (D6); the `endpoint` metric label (§ 8.1); a wire `output_text` (M2, § 6.5).
632	- QUESTION, one call per decision: answered by D10 (one hold per response, spec author's call,
633	  flagged at the gate). QUESTION, `store` retention: the operator note (D5, § 9). QUESTION, a cut
634	  function call: M5 and R15.
635	
636	Rejected: none.

# SMA-769: OpenAI Responses API ingress and tool-call interception (`/v1/responses`)

Linear: SMA-769 (parent SMA-747). Blocked by SMA-757 (merged in `ed5409fd`). Related: SMA-749 (the
tool-call model, the interceptor and the oracle), SMA-750 (Anthropic ingress), SMA-752 (policy
decisions), SMA-753 (sequence rules), SMA-755 (decision log).

This spec extends SMA-749 (`2026-11-09-sma-749-tool-call-assembler-design.md`) and SMA-757
(`2026-11-14-sma-757-oracle-argument-prefix-design.md`). Every rule of those two specs applies to
the new format unless this spec says otherwise. A reference in the form "749 § 4.3" points to
them. The spec challenge of 2026-11-14 is in § 14.

## 1. Intent

The gateway serves only `POST /v1/chat/completions`. A client that sends `POST /v1/responses`
cannot use the gateway, so its tool calls are not intercepted.

The newest OpenAI models need the Responses API for tools. On `/v1/chat/completions`, a `gpt-6`
model accepts function tools only with `reasoning_effort: "none"`. `gpt-6.1-sol` and `gpt-6-astra`
do not accept `none`, so they cannot stream tool calls on Chat Completions at all (757 § 2.4).

This change adds `POST /v1/responses`. It has the same authentication, rate limits, budget charge
and tool-call interception as `/v1/chat/completions`, for streamed and non-streamed responses.
SMA-749 lists the Responses API as a non-goal. This spec removes that non-goal.

## 2. Threat model and invariant

The threat model of 749 § 2 applies unchanged: T1 hostile model output, T2 a non-conforming
upstream, T3 the caller is not an adversary of its own agent.

**Invariant (I1, Responses form).** For every supported client parser P (§ 10.1), every tool call
that P derives from the bytes the gateway emits was decided `Allow`, with the same output index,
call id, kind, namespace, name and arguments that the decider saw. "Tool call" means every output
item that the **client** runs (§ 6.2), on every surface where P exposes it. Anything the gateway
cannot classify with certainty is not forwarded (or triggers `on_failure`).

The SMA-757 rule D2 applies from the start: at an excused client raise, every call in the client's
snapshot must match an allowed call exactly. A prefix of allowed arguments is a failure.

### 3.2 Client SDKs (read from source; nothing was executed)

Versions: **openai-python 3.48.0**, **openai-node 7.57.0**, **langchain-openai 1.8.0 with
langchain-core 1.8.0**. In openai-python, `_streaming.py` and
`lib/streaming/responses/_responses.py` are byte-identical in 3.40.0 (the version that 757 cites)
and 3.48.0.

| Aspect | openai-python 3.48.0 | openai-node 7.57.0 | LangChain 1.8.0 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Dispatch key | `data.type`; `event:` ignored | `data.type`; `event: error` raises | `chunk.type` (python raw stream) |
| Top-level truthy `error` key | raises | raises | raises (python) |
| Leading BOM | not stripped | stripped | as python |
| Last event with no blank line at EOF | dropped | flushed | as python |
| `[DONE]` | prefix match, stop | exact match, stop | as python |
| `error` event (`type: error`) | passed through | raises | raises |
| `response.failed` | passed through; `get_final_response()` raises | accumulated | raises |
| Unknown event type | passed through | raises (11 types ignored) | ignored |
| `item: null` on `added` | skipped | skipped | `AttributeError` |
| Keying | `output_index` | `output_index`; `item_id` must equal the item `id` | `item_id` first, then `output_index` |
| `*.done` events | stored apart; the live snapshot is unchanged | replace arguments, input or the whole item | ignored for `function_call`; used for `custom_tool_call` |
| Terminal `response.output` | the final response | replaces the whole snapshot | ignored for tool calls |
| Final call source | terminal `output` | the snapshot (partial at a clean EOF) | `added.arguments` + deltas (+ custom `done`); built-ins as content blocks |
| Item type check | none at terminal for a done index | skips an index it cannot find (`ResponseStream.mjs:244-250`) | none (`base.py:5615-5631`) |

The `ResponseStreamEvent` union of openai-python 3.48.0 has 59 members. With `keepalive` it has 60,
which equals the Node set (`response-accumulator.mjs:242-303`).

Consequences:

- R-a. The SDKs read a call from **different events**. Python reads the terminal `output`. Node
  reads the last of `arguments.done`, `output_item.done` and the terminal event. LangChain reads
  `added.arguments` plus the deltas. All of these views must agree, or a client runs a call that
  the decider did not see (the Responses form of 749 D9).
- R-b. No SDK checks that an index keeps its item type across views. An index that is added as
  `message` and arrives as `custom_tool_call` at `done`, or as `function_call` in the terminal
  `output`, becomes a call in all three SDKs.
- R-c. LangChain's `tool_calls` hold a partial call at every prefix (`parse_partial_json`). A call
  must never be released before it is decided.
- R-d. Python fills a missing `response.output` on `response.failed` and `response.incomplete`
  from its partial items. A terminal event without an explicit `output` array exposes partial
  calls.
- R-e. LangChain appends a `function_call_arguments.delta` to the tool call chunk at its index,
  whatever the item type. A delta event on a `custom_tool_call` or `message` item becomes call
  data.
- R-f. LangChain's source says that real traffic can report a later `output_index` on an item's
  `done` events than on its `added` event, after several built-in tool calls (`base.py:5419-5421`).
  This is not measured (M3).
- R-g. Every lifecycle event carries the whole `response` object. It echoes `instructions`,
  `tools`, `text.format.schema` and `metadata`, and the terminal event repeats every output item.
  These events can be large.

## 4. Decisions

| Id | Question | Decision |
|----|----------|----------|
| D1 | Where the format lives | A new module `paigasus-gateway-core::responses` (`classify`, `assembly`, `stream`, `body`), with its own `Protocol` implementation. It shares only the generic parts: `json`, `sse`, `report`, `interceptor`, `body`, `turn`. `ChoiceAssembly` does not change. |
| D2 | New core types | `Format::OpenAiResponses`. `HoldKey::Response` (one hold per response, D10). New `ToolCallKind` variants: `Computer`, `LocalShell`, `Shell`, `ApplyPatch`, `ToolSearch`, `McpApprovalRequest`. `function_call` uses `Function`, `custom_tool_call` uses `Custom`. `ToolCall` gets `namespace: Option<String>`. |
| D3 | Server-side state | **Stateless only.** With interception enabled (the global `[tool_interception] enabled`, that is `AppState.tool_interception` is `Some`, known before admission), a request is refused with 400 `responses-stateful-not-supported` when it has a non-null `previous_response_id`, `conversation` or `prompt`, or an `item_reference` input item. |
| D4 | Background mode | `background: true` is refused with the same 400, whether interception is enabled or not. The gateway has no route for `GET /v1/responses/{id}`, so a background result cannot be fetched through it. |
| D5 | `store` | The request body is forwarded unchanged. The gateway does not set `store: false`. D3 already stops every later turn from reading the stored output. A rewrite of `store` would be the first request rewrite (749 non-goal). Operator note: with `store` true, OpenAI keeps the output, including a blocked call, for its retention period (§ 9). |
| D6 | Service shape | One generic handler pipeline with an endpoint descriptor per route (§ 8). `/v1/chat/completions` moves to it with no change in behaviour. The descriptor is for OpenAI-shaped routes. SMA-750 decides whether it extends it. |
| D7 | Upstream | `OpenAiClient` gets one method that takes a closed `UpstreamRoute` enum (`ChatCompletions`, `Responses`), never a free path. `Responses` forwards to `{base_url}/v1/responses` with the same headers, timeouts and cancellation as chat. |
| D8 | Route switch | A new `[responses] enabled` config key, default `false`. When it is `false`, `/v1/responses` returns 404. Rollback is this key, with no deploy. |
| D9 | Streaming switch | Streaming obeys the existing `stream_enabled`. No new capability is advertised (749 D28). |
| D10 | The hold | **One hold per response.** It opens at the first client-run item's `added` frame and completes at the terminal event. The decider gets every client-run call of the response in one `decide` call, as it gets every call of choice 0 in chat. A truncation (§ 6.4, R15) blocks every call of the hold with `Truncated`. |
| D11 | Output framing | Re-framed as in 749 D3, with an `event: <data.type>` line before each `data:` line. `unframed()` uses the same form. `[DONE]` has no `event:` line. |
| D12 | Rewrite | A blocked item becomes a `message` item at the same `output_index`, frame by frame (§ 6.5). No other index changes. |
| D13 | Abort frame | A new constant for this format: `"\n\nevent: error\ndata: {\"type\":\"error\",\"code\":\"upstream-error\",\"message\":\"upstream stream error\",\"param\":null}\n\n"`. The leading blank line ends a partly sent record, as in `TERMINAL_SSE_ERROR`. |
| D14 | Billing | A Responses usage reader (§ 8.2) with no 64 KiB record limit. 749 D24 applies: a rewrite does not change the charge. |
| D15 | Size limits | Per-format limits. For Responses: `max_record_bytes` 16 MiB, `max_held_bytes` 32 MiB, and a separate `[responses] max_request_bytes` of 16 MiB. These are first values. M7 checks them, and the plan records the measured sizes. |
| D16 | Strict JSON | Per-format data subtrees and classifier keys (§ 7.1). The chat and Anthropic lists do not change (AC 8). |
| D17 | Request side | `parse_request(Format::OpenAiResponses, …)` builds `TurnFacts` (§ 7.2). |
| D18 | Client-run built-in items | Enforced like function calls (§ 6.2). They are held, decided and rewritten. |

### Reasons

- **D1.** Responses streams are item-based: each event has an `output_index` and an `item_id`, and
  `*.done` events repeat the full value. Chat Completions streams index-delta fragments. A shared
  assembly would put Responses cases into the code path that SMA-757 proved.
- **D3.** The gateway cannot see a turn that OpenAI stores. A decision then has no `prior_calls` or
  `tool_results`, and SMA-753 sequence rules fail open. A blocked call also stays in OpenAI's
  stored output, which the client never saw (M1). A `prompt` template can add tools that the
  gateway cannot see. With interception off, the gateway is a plain proxy, and these fields do no
  harm through it.
- **D8.** Billing and availability depend on shapes that are first measured in this change (M2,
  M7). An operator must be able to turn the route off without a deploy.
- **D10.** SMA-752 and SMA-753 policies that limit the calls per turn need every call of the turn
  in one decision. Chat gives them that per choice. A hold per item would give them one call at a
  time. The cost: frames after the first client-run item wait until the terminal event. Chat has
  the same cost until `finish_reason`.
- **D12.** A replacement at the same index keeps every later `output_index` valid. It needs no
  renumbering, which is the main cost of the chat rewrite.
- **D14, D15.** R-g. A lifecycle event over 64 KiB would charge only the estimate. A lifecycle
  event over 1 MiB would fail the stream, and every SDK raises without `response.created` or a
  terminal event. D3 also makes a client resend the whole conversation on every turn.
- **D18.** A shell command, a file patch or a mouse action has at least the risk of a function
  call. A report of "unenforceable" would let a client run an action that was never decided.
